allocation_sizes_at_each_limit.derivation: newcap doubles (cap ? cap*2 : 4); a big growth takes a region of max(2*new, 64 MiB); if the new size still fits the current region (new <= [d+8]) the growth is in place (nothing moves, nothing copied); only a growth past the region moves, copying element by element with no stack use, and the old region is given back after the copy; rt_veh commits up to 64 KiB per fault

ws1_oom_stack_overflow.falsifiable_next_probe: build the same B3 binary with SizeOfStackCommit raised (e.g. 1 MiB, so the stack never needs a guard-page commit during the teardown) and re-run the 512 MiB case. If the crash disappears, the mechanism is the stack guard page; if it persists, it is elsewhere. Also log the Job's PeakProcessMemoryUsed at the fault, to get the exact committed amount.
ws1_oom_stack_overflow.handler_stack_use: CONSTANT, does not depend on how much was committed: the OS exception dispatch (CONTEXT ~1.2 KiB + exception record + dispatcher frames), rt_veh's own frame (push rbx/rsi/rdi + sub rsp,96 = 120 bytes), and the VirtualAlloc/WriteFile/ExitProcess call frames; about 2-3 KiB total at every limit and every fault. What depends on the committed amount is whether the stack can GROW: the PE header sets SizeOfStackReserve 0x100000 (1 MiB) and SizeOfStackCommit 0x1000 (one page); the stack grows by guard pages, and every guard-page commit draws from the same Job limit as the kosh.

mandapa_64.fault_point: a scratch-cursor page touch in the arena at ~60 MiB of scratch (before the 1M budget: the process baseline eats a few MiB of the 64 MiB limit); stack is just mukhya's frame
mandapa_64.linux_control: without a Job limit the same program refuses E_PARIMITA at the budget (r137_mandapa.sm: 'mandape parimitat adhikam nirmmitam na sambhavati (parimitih 67108864 baait)', exit 1), confirming the budget check is real and the Windows fault is the commit, not the budget
mandapa_64.touch_control: the page-touch program refuses cleanly at 64 MiB (same limit, same handler, same message), so the crash is not 'the handler fails at 64 MiB'
mandapa_64.vs_touch: both are store faults in mukhya's frame at the 64 MiB limit; the split is plausibly the different Job-visible baselines (different programs -> different headroom), unlike B3 where the baseline is the same binary

ws1_oom_stack_overflow.second_fault: YES. After the message the only code that runs is ExitProcess(1): there is no console in the runner's children (stdout/stderr redirected to files, stdin devnull), so rt_init reads no console code page and .v_nomem skips the SetConsoleOutputCP restore (ORIGINAL_CP is 0). ExitProcess's teardown (LdrShutdownProcess, DLL detaches, heap cleanup) needs stack below the currently-committed stack, so it touches the thread's guard page, a page never committed. That commit fails because the Job limit is exhausted, and the OS raises STATUS_STACK_OVERFLOW (0xC00000FD). rt_veh correctly declines it (not 0xC0000005, and the faulting address is the stack, which the handler explicitly refuses to commit), so it is unhandled and the exit code is 0xC00000FD. The message printed; the exit did not happen.
ws1_oom_stack_overflow.the_512_split: NOT determined by the source. The 128-copy fault and the 512-copy fault are identical in every variable the source controls: same faulting instruction shape (copy-loop store near the end of the copy), same stack depth (mukhya + kosh_kship + 24 bytes of pushes), same headroom modulo 64 KiB (handler commits 64 KiB per fault; old backings 64/256 MiB and limits 128/512 MiB are all multiples of 64 KiB; baseline is the same binary), same handler path. If the crash were determined by any of those, 128 and 512 would behave the same; they do not (6/6, deterministically, serially). The distinguishing variable is outside the compiler's emitted code and the handler; leading candidates are the exact Job-visible baseline commit (which sets the absolute headroom - the teardown needs a whole 4 KiB page) or the committed stack high-water mark at the fault. Neither can be computed from the source, and no guess is presented as the mechanism.

copy_loop_answers.existing_file: OVERWRITE, unconditionally ([IO.File]::Copy($src,$dst,$true)); no skip, no fail, no branch in the copy loop at all
copy_loop_answers.hash_after_write: NO post-write hash check anywhere in the copy path; Verify-Payload hashes the STAGE before copying, the guard hashes OLD files before copying; the hang is not a post-write check
copy_loop_answers.open_while_held: the loop opens each destination with FileShare.None and no lock check; in the same-directory upgrade Remove-ManifestFiles runs first so most destinations do not exist at copy time, but files NOT in the old manifest still exist and are overwritten blindly; if another process holds a destination, File.Copy THROWS, it does not hang

ws2_same_directory_upgrade.expectation_correction: the A3 expectation ('installer refuses over existing install') was wrong about the source's contract: same-folder upgrade is allowed, a different folder is refused
ws2_same_directory_upgrade.stall_location: engine log last entry 'Copied 100 of 658 files; last: docs\_newchapter_en.html' at 21:32:45 (658 = 657 payload + manifest); partial tree held 117 files; snapshot found docs\reports\EDGE-COVERAGE-30.md unreadable because another process held it open (the installer itself, mid-copy - File.Copy holds the destination open with FileShare.None). So the copy stalled inside Copy-StagedFiles between files 101 and ~117, with a destination file open; the log, naming only every 100th file AFTER copying, cannot say which one
ws2_same_directory_upgrade.why_not_in_the_code: the copy loop contains no wait, no retry, and no lock-acquisition: File.Copy either completes in milliseconds or throws; nothing in install-core.ps1 can block for five minutes inside that loop. At 21:38:15 all 27 threads of the PowerShell child (PID 27748) were Wait/Suspended and the wizard's threads (PID 36956) likewise - a whole-process-tree suspension no code in the installer or wizard can produce (the wizard only waits on the child handle with a 15-minute timeout, then terminates it; it creates the child with CREATE_NO_WINDOW and no redirected pipes, so no pipe deadlock and no console to block on). The Windows report says the suspension's cause 'has not been established' and 'does not prove a product-code deadlock'; concurred, not reclassified. The hang is reproducible on demand (run the installer at the existing install folder), which makes it fixable, but the fix is not in the copy loop's logic. What the source DOES show is missing: a per-file START log (so the next stall names the file it stopped on) and copying to a unique temporary file with hash verification before publishing (R207's design - so a stall never leaves a half-written destination open and a retry can resume). The 15-minute timeout was never observed (owner ended the wizard first; orphan child needed separate cleanup).
